## Briefing

::: {.rq-lesson}
Read first: [Grammar of Graphics](../data-visualization/ggplot_grammar.qmd) and the [Basic Plot Gallery](../plot-gallery/basic.qmd). A ggplot is **data** + **aesthetic mappings** (`aes()`: which variable goes to x, y, colour) + **geoms** (the marks), plus labels, facets and themes.
:::


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
ggplot(ncd, aes(x = salt_g, y = sbp, colour = sex)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.6) +
  facet_wrap(~ residence) +
  labs(x = "Salt intake (g/day)", y = "Systolic BP (mmHg)")
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![](b4_first_plots_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-2-1.png){width=800}
:::
:::


::: {.rq-lesson}
**Choose by variable type.** One continuous variable: histogram. Counts of a category: bar chart. A continuous variable across groups: box plots. Two continuous variables: scatter plot. Put a fixed colour *outside* `aes()`; inside, it is treated as data.
:::

## Level 1 · Which plot? {.rq-level}

You want to show how many adults are in each education level. Which plot fits best?

- A histogram of the education level of each adult
- A bar chart with one bar per education level
- A line chart joining the education levels in order
- A scatter plot of education level against id
:::

::: {.rq-item data-id="b4-02" data-world="b4" data-type="mcq" data-diff="1" data-tags="plot-choice" data-hash="ruo2c0.up4ta6" data-show="QSBib3ggcGxvdCBvZiBTQlAgZm9yIGVhY2ggZWR1Y2F0aW9uIGxldmVs" data-explain="QSBjb250aW51b3VzIG91dGNvbWUgYWNyb3NzIGdyb3VwczogYm94IHBsb3RzIHNob3cgdGhlIG1lZGlhbiwgc3ByZWFkIGFuZCBvdXRsaWVycyBvZiBlYWNoIGdyb3VwIHNpZGUgYnkgc2lkZS4=" data-hints="WyJZb3UgbmVlZCB0aGUgc3ByZWFkLCBub3QganVzdCBhIGNvdW50IG9yIGEgc2luZ2xlIG1lYW4uIl0="}
You want to compare the spread of systolic BP across the four education levels. Which plot fits best?

- A box plot of SBP for each education level
- A single histogram of SBP for the whole sample
- A bar chart of the number of adults per level
- A pie chart of the mean SBP of each education level
:::

::: {.rq-item data-id="b4-04" data-world="b4" data-type="mcq" data-diff="1" data-tags="ggplot" data-hash="ruostg.up5m8y" data-show="SXQgbWFwcyBhZ2UgdG8gdGhlIHggcG9zaXRpb24gYW5kIHNicCB0byB0aGUgeSBwb3NpdGlvbg==" data-explain="YWVzKCkgbWFwcyB2YXJpYWJsZXMgdG8gdmlzdWFsIHByb3BlcnRpZXMgKGhlcmUgeCBhbmQgeSBwb3NpdGlvbikuIFRoZSBnZW9tIGRyYXdzIHRoZSBtYXJrczsgZGF0YSwgbWFwcGluZ3MsIGdlb21zLCBzY2FsZXMgYW5kIHRoZW1lcyBhcmUgc2VwYXJhdGUgbGF5ZXJzLg==" data-hints="WyJhZXMgc3RhbmRzIGZvciBhZXN0aGV0aWMgbWFwcGluZy4iXQ=="}
In ggplot(ncd, aes(x = age, y = sbp)) + geom_point(), what does the aes() part do?

- It draws one point for every row of the data in the plot
- It filters ncd to the two columns that are used
- It maps age to the x position and sbp to the y position
- It chooses the colours and the theme used for the plot
:::

## Level 2 · Grammar details {.rq-level}


::: {.rq-item data-id="b4-03" data-world="b4" data-type="mcq" data-diff="2" data-tags="ggplot" data-hash="ruofks.up57rm" data-show="T25lIGRlZmF1bHQgY29sb3VyLCBwbHVzIGEgbGVnZW5kIGxhYmVsbGVkIGJsdWU=" data-explain="SW5zaWRlIGFlcygpLCAiYmx1ZSIgaXMgdHJlYXRlZCBhcyBkYXRhIChhIGNvbnN0YW50IGNhdGVnb3J5KSwgc28gZ2dwbG90IHBpY2tzIGl0cyBmaXJzdCBkZWZhdWx0IGNvbG91ciBhbmQgYWRkcyBhIGxlZ2VuZC4gVG8gc2V0IGEgY29sb3VyLCBwdXQgY29sb3VyID0gImJsdWUiIG91dHNpZGUgYWVzKCku" data-hints="WyJhZXMoKSBtYXBzIGRhdGEgdG8gbG9va3M7IGlzIFwiYmx1ZVwiIGRhdGEgaGVyZT8iXQ=="}
```r
ggplot(ncd, aes(age, sbp)) + geom_point(aes(colour = "blue"))
```
What do you get?

- Blue points with no legend, as the code intends
- An error, because colours cannot go inside aes()
- Points coloured by a variable in ncd called blue
- One default colour, plus a legend labelled blue
:::

::: {.rq-item data-id="b4-05" data-world="b4" data-type="mcq" data-diff="2" data-tags="ggplot" data-hash="rup624.up60qa" data-show="SXQgc3BsaXRzIHRoZSBwbG90IGludG8gc21hbGwgcGFuZWxzLCBvbmUgcGVyIGdyb3Vw" data-explain="RmFjZXRzIHNwbGl0IHRoZSBkYXRhIGludG8gc21hbGwgbXVsdGlwbGVzLCBvbmUgcGFuZWwgcGVyIGxldmVsLCB3aXRoIHNoYXJlZCBheGVzIHNvIHRoZSBwYW5lbHMgY2FuIGJlIGNvbXBhcmVkLg==" data-hints="WyJGYWNldCBtZWFucyBwYW5lbC4iXQ=="}
What does adding + facet_wrap(~ residence) to a scatter plot of age against sbp do?

- It colours the points by residence in one shared panel
- It splits the plot into small panels, one per group
- It drops the adults whose residence value is missing
- It adds a separate trend line for each residence group
:::

::: {.rq-item data-id="b4-06" data-world="b4" data-type="order" data-diff="1" data-tags="ggplot" data-hash="ms24o5.s298po" data-show="" data-explain="RGF0YSwgdGhlbiBtYXBwaW5ncywgdGhlbiBnZW9tcyB0aGF0IGRyYXcgdGhlbSwgdGhlbiBsYWJlbHMgYW5kIGZpbmFsbHkgdGhlIG92ZXJhbGwgbG9vay4=" data-hints="WyJZb3UgY2Fubm90IGRyYXcgcG9pbnRzIGJlZm9yZSBzYXlpbmcgd2hpY2ggdmFyaWFibGVzIGdvIHdoZXJlLiJd"}
Put the layers of a ggplot in the order you usually write them:

1. Finish with a theme, such as theme_minimal()
1. Map variables to x, y and colour with aes()
1. Start with ggplot() and the data
1. Add the geometric layer, such as geom_point()
1. Add labels for the axes and title with labs()
:::
